newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn intelligence head warns of Mideast missiles.
newsitem.headline: Bonn intelligence head warns of Mideast missiles.

text.p: Several Mideast countries may have the capability to launch middle-distance missile strikes at central Europe within the next decade, the head of Germany's intelligence agency said on Sunday.

Hansjoerg Geiger, head of the Bundesnachrichtendienst, said in a television interview that several countries in the region were working on developing the missiles as well as ABC weapons -- atomic, biological and chemical weapons -- for warheads.

"We have to be realistic and assume that some countries will have missiles at the latest by 2008 to 2010 that could reach Central Europe," Geiger said in an interview with German television's second channel ZDF.
He did not name any countries, but said that since the end of the Cold War some nations had been actively working on improving their missile technology.
Geiger said that was one reason why his agency, which some government officials say is superfluous with the end of the Cold War, should not be dismantled.
"We need an intelligence agency," Geiger said. "We have left the bi-polar world. There are now crises in the entire world. And an intelligence agency serves to assist the government."
The agency has about 6,000 employees and is in the process of eliminating 700 jobs.
